## 3. Red flags

### 1. [HIGH] Weekly hours are above what a student may work

The form says 33 hours per week. No student permit allows more than 30 hours, and most students may work 10 to 20 hours. Working above the permitted hours can lead to a fine, a visa problem and trouble for the employer.

> Korean: 근무요일 및 시간 : 월~금 18:00 ~ 23:00, 토 10:00 ~ 18:00 (주 33시간)  (quote matched to scan: yes)

- [ ] real problem  - [ ] not a problem (false alarm)  - [ ] explanation correct  - [ ] severity right

### 2. [HIGH] Hourly wage below the legal minimum

The hourly wage is 9,000 KRW. The legal minimum wage is 10,320 KRW per hour in 2026. Paying less is not allowed, even if you agree to it. Ask for a correction or contact the Ministry of Employment and Labor (call 1350).

> Korean: 시급 : 9,000원      임금지급방법 : 현금  (quote matched to scan: yes)

- [ ] real problem  - [ ] not a problem (false alarm)  - [ ] explanation correct  - [ ] severity right

### 3. [HIGH] Work started before the permit

The form says work has already started. A student must receive the part-time work permit BEFORE starting. Working earlier can be punished, for the student (visa problems, fine) and for the employer. Stop and check with your school.

### Risks to Be Aware Of:
- **Incomplete Information:** The document is missing signatures from the school student affairs officer and the approval number from the immigration office. This could cause delays or issues if you need to present this document elsewhere.
- **Employment Period:** The employment period is from September 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027. Ensure you understand the exact dates and any potential extensions or changes.
- **Payment Method:** The payment is in cash. While this is common in some small businesses, it's important to ensure that the employer is reputable and that you are paid on time and in full.
- **Compliance:** Ensure that the employer is following all legal requirements for part-time employment, especially regarding working hours and breaks.

If you have any doubts or need further assistance, it's a good idea to consult with your school's international student office or a legal advisor.
